web_evidence.title: Jodi Picoult · Leaving Time (2014)
web_evidence.note: The author's authorized excerpt presents separately headed Jenna and Alice opening sections; both sustain participating narration with I, me, my, and we.

web_evidence.title: Jodi Picoult Writing Styles in Leaving Time
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly states that the novel is told in first person by Alice, Jenna, Virgil, and Serenity and maps those narrators across the chapters.

web_evidence.title: LEAVING TIME | Kirkus Reviews
web_evidence.note: Kirkus identifies the complete narrating ensemble: Jenna shares narrative duties with Virgil, Serenity, and Alice. This corroborates that the many interior first-person quotes belong to the novel's controlling narrators. It identifies the narrating ensemble but does not explicitly establish grammatical person.

web_evidence.title: Review by mirkatte - Leaving Time | The StoryGraph
web_evidence.note: A detailed reader review explicitly identifies Alice, Jenna, Serenity, and Virgil as the book's four first-person narrators, including the audiobook's separate voice for each. This unvetted reader review is discovery-level corroboration, not an independent authoritative structural source.

person_note: The book uses multiple participating narrators, but all controlling strands are first person: Jenna, Alice, Serenity, and Virgil narrate their own sections as I. The Goodreads evidence repeatedly exposes first-person event narration across present-day investigation, psychic material, and Alice's sustained elephant-research and relationship history; dialogue, aphorisms, generic you passages, and the author's note were not allowed to vote. The authorized opening independently shows named first-person sections for Jenna and Alice, while whole-book sources identify the same four-narrator structure and explicitly describe all four as first person. Multiple first-person narrators therefore yield FIRST, not ALTERNATING. No credible source indicates sustained second- or third-person base sections; the main limitation is that the Tier A excerpt covers only the opening, offset by extensive interior quote evidence and whole-book structural descriptions. Source audit: the reader review is Tier D and the Kirkus ensemble description is structural context only; FIRST remains supported by diagnostic quotes, the authorized excerpt, and the explicit whole-book POV guide.
